name: Democratic People's Republic of Korea

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 120,410 km2 (World Bank AG.LND.TOTL.K2); high adds ~3% for inland water.

population.note: asOf 2025: 26,571,036 (World Bank). Range allows for 2026 change.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.277 as quoted: 1,280,000 active. CIA Factbook 2025: up to 1.3 million. World Bank 1,469,000 (2020) includes paramilitary. ~11,000-15,000 troops deployed to Russia (Kursk) 2024-25 are counted.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: 600,000 reserves. High is an educated allowance for the better-trained part of the Worker-Peasant Red Guards (5.7 million, paramilitary) and Reserve Military Training Units (ROK MND: 7.62 million reserves of all kinds).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 1,280,000 minus infantry P roles 650,000 = 630,000. Navy (~60,000 per US DoD 2014), Air and Anti-Air Force, Strategic Force, artillery and armour crews, construction/logistics units.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Total-war garrison state: 1.28 million active (4.8% of population) plus militias claimed at ~7.6 million; 20% (~5.3 million) is a sustained full mobilisation comparable to WWII peaks.

count.note: Educated guess. Ground force ~1.1 million (ROK/US estimates as quoted); ~80 infantry divisions/brigades plus mechanised corps. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_People%27s_Army_Ground_Force)

quality.note: Rubric 0.25: older small arms; some modern kit seen in Russia.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: very long conscription, drill-heavy, limited live-fire.

count.note: Educated guess. Special operations forces and light infantry brigades (often cited ~200,000). Worker-Peasant Red Guards (5.7 million) excluded. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_People%27s_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: ~200,000 special operations/light infantry, intensively trained.

ROK MND 2018: 2,500 armoured vehicles; US DoD 2014: 2,200; KPA article: 2,100.

count.note: Educated guess. Batteries: dense IADS of SA-2/3/5 sites, KN-06 (Pongae-5), mobile SAMs and ~11,000 AA guns (KPA article). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_People%27s_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: 10-year conscripts, little live-fire training (fuel shortages); some combat experience from troops sent to Russia (Kursk 2024-25).

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: rigid, politicised command; some modern combat experience gained in Russia 2024-25.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: indoctrinated long-service conscripts, harsh discipline.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: regime-driven fanatical home defence; hunger and desertion lower it in a long war.

weapons.note: Anchor 8-9 mix: ICBMs/hypersonic IRBM and KN-23 are anchor-10-class; bulk of guns and small arms anchor 8.

armor.note: Anchor 8: T-55/T-62 derivatives; few Chonma-20 with modern features. audit 2026-10-30: mid 7.8 -> 8.3: the tech scale is absolute equipment level, so it may not fall within a lineage; T-55/T-62 derivatives (1958-61 designs, interpolated ~8.4 between the 1943 and 1985 anchors) are above the 1950 T-34/85 (7.9).

ships.note: Anchor 8: small craft, Romeo submarines; new Choe Hyon destroyers anchor 9.

fortification.note: Anchor 9: massive hardened artillery sites (HARTS), tunnels, underground air bases.

logistics.note: Anchor 7-8: rail-dependent, chronic fuel shortage. audit 2026-10-30: mid 7.4 -> 7.6: the tech scale is absolute equipment level, so it may not fall within a lineage; the rail net and truck park exceed those of 1950 (7.5); fuel shortage is a supply limit, not equipment.

isr.note: Anchor 8 plus: first reconnaissance satellite (Malligyong-1, 2023), few drones.

air.note: Anchor 8: MiG-17/19/21 copies; MiG-29 anchor 9. audit 2026-10-30: mid 7.4 -> 8.4: the tech scale is absolute equipment level, so it may not fall within a lineage; MiG-17/19/21 copies (1950s designs, ~8.3-8.5 by year) and a few MiG-29 (anchor 9) are above the 1950 Yak-9 and Il-10 (7.8).

cyber.note: Anchor 10 minus: Lazarus/Reconnaissance General Bureau - among the most active state cyber forces.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. No World Bank GDP. CIA Factbook 2023: real GDP $15.4 billion and $600 per capita in 2015 dollars (market-exchange-rate-like; used as low). Bank of Korea estimates (not fetched) imply ~$1,200-1,400 nominal per capita; PPP 2011 int$ higher. (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/east-n-southeast-asia/kn.json)

gdp.note: Population 26,571,036 x GDP per capita 600 / 1,300 / 2,000 (educated guess).

milSpendShare.note: CIA Factbook: military expenditures estimated at 20-30% of GDP annually 2010-2020; 2024 state budget ~16% on defence. Mid is an educated point.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. No World Bank data; Bank of Korea sectoral estimates (not fetched) put mining, manufacturing and construction at roughly a third of output. (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/east-n-southeast-asia/kn.json)

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PRK/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 54.1% (2025). s = 4.78 Mt 2024 crop (RDA, https://koreatimes.co.kr/www/nation/2025/03/103_393434.html) / 5.76 Mt FAO requirement (https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/nation/2024/08/103_380552.html) = 0.83. Mid 1 - 0.541/0.83 = 0.35. Low: a 0.60, s 0.78 (flood year) = 0.23. High: a 0.50, s 0.84 (4.82 Mt 2023) = 0.40. This surplus is what state procurement takes for the PDS and the army. Import dependence: chronic deficit of ~1 Mt a year. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 0.0 -> 0.35, rule changed: value is the share of production not eaten by the farm population, import dependence goes in the note.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 13,154,539 x share of males aged 15-19 6.336% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 166,707. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

armor.note: Educated guess. Ryu Kyong-su tank factory (Chonma-20). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Korean_People%27s_Army_Ground_Force)

artillery.note: Educated guess. Large gun/MRL and shell output (shells exported to Russia). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Korean_People%27s_Army_Ground_Force)

missiles.note: Educated guess. TELs per year; Hwasong-11 launchers 250 delivered in 2024. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Korean_People%27s_Army_Ground_Force)

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Choe Hyon-class at Nampo/Chongjin. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_People%27s_Navy)

drones.note: Educated guess. Group 2+ incl. Russian-assisted lines (reported). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_People%27s_Army_Air_Force)

roadKm.note: asOf 2006: 25,554 km total, only 724 km paved (mid). Engineered unpaved military roads make the high relevant.

railKm.note: asOf 1999: 5,214 route-km (World Bank). World Bank value from 1999; CIA Factbook 7,435 km (2014, ~5,400 electrified) as high. Rail is the backbone of military logistics.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 10 ports, none large or medium, 7 small (Chongjin, Haeju, Hungnam, Najin, Nampo, Sonbong, Wonsan) = mid.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Below the merchant-capacity list threshold; Factbook 2023: 264 ships, mostly general cargo; sanctions evasion uses foreign flags. (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/east-n-southeast-asia/kn.json)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Rail-dependent, fuel-short logistics; planned to sustain offensive operations only ~100 km into South Korea.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen and horses used in agriculture (not from FAO data); KPA has some pack units.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026: ~60 assembled warheads (stockpile); fissile material may suffice for up to ~90 (high).

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: mountainous, extensively tunnelled and fortified, harsh winters, total regime-enforced population mobilisation.

notes: Modern snapshot asOf 2025-26. All figures for the DPRK are estimates: personnel from IISS 2026, equipment from ROK MND 2018 and US DoD 2014 reports as quoted on Wikipedia, air force types from the KPAF article's inventory table (grade C). GDP: no World Bank data; educated range (grade D). Population: World Bank 2025 (UN-based). Doctrine archetype-coldwar-soviet: Soviet-model mass army with huge artillery park. ~11,000-15,000 KPA troops fought for Russia in Kursk 2024-25 and North Korean shells and KN-23/24 missiles are used in Ukraine. Worker-Peasant Red Guards and other paramilitary (IISS 5,889,000) excluded.
